blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Deep learning models for whole-body positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) hold significant clinical potential for disease detection, treatment planning, and response assessment. However, the time and cost associated with expert annotations remain major bottlenecks in developing robust and generalizable models. Although self-supervised learning (SSL) has emerged as a promising approach to mitigating annotation scarcity, its application to whole-body PET/CT remains relatively underexplored due to the limited availability of large-scale datasets and the challenges associated with learning complementary cross-modal representations. To address these limitations, we curate a heterogeneous, multi-tracer, multi-institutional cohort comprising 6,531 whole-body PET/CT scans and propose LoRe-MIM (Lost-Or-Replaced Masked Image Modelling), a novel self-supervised framework designed to learn multimodal representations through masked image reconstruction. Specifically, LoRe-MIM introduces a masking strategy in which image regions are either replaced with zeros (Lost) or substituted with corresponding complementary imaging modality (Replaced), encouraging the model to capture both modality-specific characteristics and cross-modal relationships. We evaluate the learned representations across multiple downstream tasks, including multimodal PET/CT image reconstruction, patch-based classification into cancer vs. non-cancer, whole-body lesion segmentation, label-efficient training, and robustness assessment. Experimental results demonstrate that LoRe-MIM consistently outperforms the corresponding state-of-the-art baselines across these tasks, highlighting its potential as a scalable and generalizable self-supervised learning framework for whole-body PET/CT analysis.
blocks.zh: 全身正体排放成像学/复合成像学(PET/CT)的深层学习模型在疾病检测、治疗规划和反应评估方面具有巨大的临床潜力。 然而,与专家说明有关的时间和费用仍然是发展强有力和可通用模式的主要瓶颈。 尽管自我监督的学习(SSL)已成为缓解注解稀缺性的有希望的方法,但由于大规模数据集有限,与学习互补的跨模式表述有关的挑战,其对全身PET/CT的应用仍然相对不足. 为了克服这些限制,我们管理了一个由6,531个全身PET/CT扫描组成的多机构组合,并提议Lore-MIM(丢失或被替换的相片模型),这是一个新的自我监督框架,旨在通过蒙面相片重建学习多模式表述。 具体地说,LoRe-MIM引入了一种遮掩策略,即图像区域要么被取而代之为零(Lost),要么被取而代之的是相应的互补成像模式(被取而代之),鼓励模型既捕捉模式特定特征又捕捉到跨模式关系. 我们评价在多个下游任务中汲取的教训,包括多模式PET/CT图像重建、基于补丁的癌症与非癌症的分类、全身损伤分解、标签效率高的培训以及强健性评估。 实验结果表明,LoRe-MIM在所有这些任务中的业绩始终超过相应的最先进的基线,突出了它作为全身PET/CT分析的可扩展和可概括的自我监督学习框架的潜力。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Cancerous lesions in whole-body imaging exhibit substantial morphological variability in their physical appearance, shape, size, and structural characteristics across patients, cancer types, and anatomical sites [ 14 , 26 , 22 ] . Noninvasive imaging technologies such as positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) play a critical role in detecting such lesions, determining disease stage, guiding treatment planning, and assessing treatment response [ 41 ] . PET captures the molecular and physiological activity of lesions, whereas CT provides complementary anatomical and structural context. However, with the rising global cancer burden [ 38 ] , the volume of whole-body PET/CT examinations is increasing at a substantially faster pace than the availability of expert nuclear medicine specialists capable of interpreting them. This growing imbalance creates a critical need for automated systems that can efficiently and accurately analyze large volumes of whole-body PET/CT scans and assist clinicians. As in many other medical imaging domains, deep-learning-based methods have emerged as a promising approach for automating oncologic whole-body PET/CT interpretation [ 10 , 16 , 32 ] .
blocks.zh: 全身成像中的癌症损伤在患者、癌症类型和解剖地点的外观、外形、体积和结构特征方面表现出了巨大的形态变化[14、26、22]。 非侵入性成像技术,如正电子排放成像法/复合成像法(PET/CT),在检测这种损伤、确定疾病阶段、指导治疗规划以及评估治疗反应[41]方面发挥着关键作用。 PET捕捉损伤的分子和生理活性,而CT则提供互补的解剖和结构上下文. 然而,随着全球癌症负担的上升[38],全身PET/CT检查量的增加速度大大快于能够解释这些检查的专家。 这种日益严重的不平衡导致迫切需要自动化系统,能够高效和准确地分析大量全身PET/CT扫描和协助临床医生。 与许多其他医学成像领域一样,深入学习的方法已成为实现肿瘤全体PET/CT解释自动化的一种有希望的方法[10、16、32]。

blocks.en: Deep-learning-based models have been developed for whole-body lesion segmentation [ 43 , 3 , 18 , 12 , 9 , 23 , 44 , 21 , 25 ] and patch-level classifications tasks (cancer presence or absence) [ 35 , 27 , 34 , 1 , 40 , 45 , 1 , 33 , 29 ] . The accuracy and generalizability of deep learning methods for both tasks depend heavily on the ability of the learned PET/CT imaging representations to distinguish between cancer and non-cancer voxels, capture diversity and heterogeneity in imaging features across patient populations, cancer types, tracers, scanners, and anatomical sites, and the robustness to noise, registration errors, and missing modality. Two straightforward approaches to learning such representations are supervised training with task-specific annotations and transfer learning from a model pretrained on a related domain.
blocks.zh: 为全身损伤分解[43,3,18,12,9,23,44,21,25]和补丁级分类任务(癌症存在与否)开发了深层学习模式[35,27,34,1,40,45,1,33,29]. 这两项任务的深入学习方法的准确性和可概括性在很大程度上取决于所学的PET/CT成像表现方法能否区分癌症和非癌症的活体,能否在成像特征中捕捉到患者群体、癌症类型、跟踪仪、扫描仪和解剖站点的多样性和异质性,以及噪音的强性、登记错误和缺失模式。 学习这种表述的两种直截了当的方法是监督培训,并附有具体任务说明,以及从预先在相关领域培训的模式中转学。

blocks.en: Supervised deep learning approaches have been extensively investigated for lesion segmentation in whole-body PET/CT imaging [ 43 , 3 , 18 , 12 , 9 , 23 , 44 , 21 , 25 ] . Blanc-Durand et al. [ 3 ] employed a 3D U-Net architecture for the automated detection and segmentation of lymphoma lesions in whole-body FDG-PET/CT scans. Jemaa et al. [ 18 ] introduced a multi-stage segmentation framework combining 2D segmentation, connected-component analysis, and 3D segmentation-based refinement to improve lesion delineation in whole-body FDG-PET/CT images. To facilitate advancements in whole-body tumor segmentation, Gatidis et al. [ 9 ] organized the AutoPET-II challenge and made publicly available a collection of whole-body FDG-PET/CT scans representing diverse tumor types. Building upon this dataset, He et al. [ 12 ] incorporated camouflaged object detection strategies, while Liu et al. [ 23 ] developed hybrid Mamba-CNN architectures for automated lesion detection and segmentation. Although FDG remains the predominant radiotracer in deep learning-based whole-body PET/CT segmentation research, alternative tracers, including 68 Ga-Pentixafor [ 43 ] and prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA)-targeted tracers [ 44 , 21 ] , have also been investigated in some studies. Specifically, Xu et al. [ 43 ] designed a cascaded W-Net architecture comprising two V-Nets [ 25 ] , where the first network processes CT images and the second integrates 68 Ga-Pentixafor PET with CT information for whole-body multiple myeloma detection. For whole-body PSMA-PET/CT lesion segmentation, Li et al. [ 21 ] proposed a hybrid 3D Transformer–CNN framework, whereas Xu et al. [ 44 ] employed U-Net-based architectures. Collectively, these supervised PET/CT segmentation approaches leverage whole-body imaging to identify and delineate lesions associated with single or multiple tumor types.
blocks.zh: 对全身PET/CT成像中的损伤分解进行了广泛调查[43、3、18、12、9、23、44、21、25]。 布兰克-杜兰德等. [3] 在全身FDG-PET/CT扫描中使用了3D U-Net架构来自动检测和分解淋巴瘤损伤. 杰马等. [18] 引入了多相分解框架,结合了2D分解,连接组件分析,并基于3D分解的改进,以改善全身FDG-PET/CT图像中的损伤分解. 为了促进全身肿瘤分化的进步,Gatidis等人。 [9] 组织了AutoPET-II挑战,并公开提供了代表了多种肿瘤类型的全身FDG-PET/CT扫描. 根据该数据集,He等. [12] 加入了伪装物体探测策略,而刘等. [23]开发了混合的曼巴-CNN架构,用于自动化损伤检测和分解. 虽然FDG仍然是深层以学习为基础的全体PET/CT分解研究中最主要的放射素,但一些研究中也调查了替代的痕量,包括68个Ga-Pentixafor [43]和前列腺特有膜抗原[44,21]目标痕量. 具体而言,许等. [43]设计了由两个V-Net[25]组成的级联W-Net架构,其中第一个网络处理CT图像,第二个网络将68 Ga-Pentixafor PET与CT信息集成,用于全身多个肌瘤检测. 关于全身PSMA-PET/CT损伤分解,Li等。 [21] 提出了混合3D变形器-CNN框架,而徐等. [44] 采用了基于U-Net的架构。 集体而言,这些受监督的PET/CT分解方法利用全身成像来识别并划定与单一或多类肿瘤有关的损伤。

blocks.en: Similar to lesion segmentation, earlier works on lesion classification relied on supervised training of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) [ 35 , 27 , 34 , 1 ] , whereas several recent works [ 40 , 45 , 1 , 33 , 29 ] have explored transfer learning from pretrained models. Sibille et al. proposed a CNN to localize foci of increased FDG uptake and classify lesions suspicious for lung cancer [ 35 ] . Mu et al. developed a supervised convolutional network using FDG PET/CT scans to classify epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutation status in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) [ 27 ] . Shao et al. trained a dual-stream 3D CNN using 18 F-FDG PET/CT to distinguish benign and invasive adenocarcinoma in ground-glass lung nodules [ 34 ] . Alves et al. investigated three 3D CNN architectures inspired by the classical 2D architectures AlexNet [ 20 ] , VGGNet [ 37 ] , and Inception-v2 [ 39 ] for pulmonary nodule classification using 18 F-FDG PET/CT images [ 1 ] . They also investigated transfer learning from ResNet-50 [ 13 ] pretrained on ImageNet [ 7 ] . Tao et al. proposed an ensemble ResNet-based classification framework that leveraged transfer learning to extract features from CT, PET, and fused PET/CT images, integrating individual classifiers through majority voting for lung tumor diagnosis [ 40 ] . Yang et al. investigated six ImageNet-pretrained CNN architectures for distinguishing metastatic and lymphomatous cervical lymph nodes using PET/CT images, employing both fine-tuned CNN classifiers and pretrained deep feature extractors combined with support vector machines [ 45 ] . Nishigaki et al. fine-tuned a Vision Transformer (ViT) pretrained on ImageNet-21k to classify benign and malignant slices from 18 F-FDG PET/CT scans, demonstrating superior performance compared with pretrained CNN architectures, including DenseNet and EfficientNet [ 29 ] . Recognizing the limitations of transferring representations learned from 2D natural images to 3D medical imaging, Shao et al. explored transfer learning from Models Genesis for predicting EGFR mutation status in NSCLC patients [ 33 ] .
blocks.zh: 与损伤分解类似,早期的损伤分解工作依赖于对进化神经网络(CNNs)的有监督的训练[35,27,34,1],而近期的多部作品[40,45,1,33,29]则探索了从被预先训练的模型中进行转移学习. 西比尔等. 提议CNN将FDG摄入量增加的症结本地化,并对肺癌疑似损伤进行分类[35]. Mu等利用FDG PET/CT扫描器开发出有监督的分解网络,将非小细胞肺癌患者的表皮生长因子受体(EGFR)突变状态分类[27]. 绍等. 利用18个F-FDG PET/CT培训了双流三维有线电视新闻网,以区分地玻璃肺结核中的良性和入侵性腺癌[34]。 Alves等调查了由古典2D架构所激发出的三个3D CNN架构 AlexNet [20],VGGNet [37],和Inception-v2 [39] 肺结核分级使用18个F-FDG PET/CT图像 [1]. 他们还调查了从ResNet-50[13]在ImageNet上预先培训的转学学习[7]. Tao等人提出了基于群策群力的ResNet分类框架,利用转移学习从CT,PET中取出特征,并结合了PET/CT图像,通过对肺瘤诊断的多数投票整合了个人分类器[40]. Yang等调查了使用PET/CT图像区分元静脉和淋巴宫颈淋巴结的6个被ImageNet预先训练的CNN架构,同时使用精细的CNN分级器和被预先训练的深层特征提取器与辅助向量机结合[45]. Nishigaki等人在ImageNet-21k上对一款Vision Transformer(ViT)进行了微调,从18个F-FDG PET/CT扫描中将良性和恶性切片分类,与包括DenseNet和高效Net在内的经过预训的CNN架构相比表现出了优异的性能. Shao等人认识到将从2D自然图像中汲取的表达法转移到3D医学成像的局限性,探索了从Models Genesis中进行转移学习,以预测NSCLC患者的EGFR突变状态[33].

blocks.en: As observed in existing whole-body PET/CT studies, lesion segmentation is commonly formulated as a fully supervised dense prediction task, whereas lesion classification often leverages representations transferred from models pretrained on large external datasets such as ImageNet or natural-image foundation models. Supervised learning, however, is constrained by the difficulty of constructing sufficiently large and diverse annotated datasets, as reliable lesion-level and voxel-level annotations are expensive to obtain and require substantial sub-speciality clinical expertise. Transfer learning from the 2D natural-image domain to 3D medical imaging introduces a different limitation: a substantial domain mismatch arising from differences in image dimensionality, visual appearance, intensity distributions, and underlying anatomical and functional characteristics.
blocks.zh: 正如现有的全身PET/CT研究所观察到的那样,损伤分解通常被表述为完全监督的密集预测任务,而损伤分解则往往利用在ImageNet或自然图像基础模型等大型外部数据集上预先培训的模型中转移的表示。 然而,由于难以建立足够大和多样的附加说明的数据集,监督学习受到限制,因为可靠的损伤级和活体级说明成本昂贵,需要大量的亚专业临床专业知识。 从2D自然成像域向3D医学成像的学习转移引入了不同的限制:由于图像维度,视觉外观,强度分布,以及基础解剖学和功能特征的差异而产生出巨大的域不匹配.

blocks.en: Self-supervised pretraining offers a unified alternative by exploiting large collections of unlabeled PET/CT scans to learn domain-specific representations that can subsequently be adapted to segmentation through fine-tuning or used as feature extractors for lesion classification. In recent years, several studies have explored self-supervised pretraining for whole-body PET/CT lesion analysis [ 46 , 30 , 15 , 19 , 24 ] . Yazdani et al. adopted self-supervised SwinUNETR pretraining using 752 whole-body [ 68 Ga ] [^{68}\mathrm{Ga}] -PSMA-11 PET/CT scans for prostate cancer metastasis segmentation and demonstrated the benefit of pretraining for downstream lesion delineation [ 46 ] . Oh et al. applied contrastive-learning-based pretraining using 1,292 samples from the publicly available AutoPET III dataset and evaluated its benefit for both lesion segmentation and staging classification on a private institutional cohort [ 30 ] . Huang et al. proposed a modality-complementary masking strategy to learn cross-modal PET/CT representations using 507 FDG cases from AutoPET III [ 15 ] . Liu et al. similarly adopted modality-complementary masking for an FDG-focused foundation model pretrained on 4,997 scans [ 24 ] . Keshavarz et al. employed multimodal SwinUNETR pretraining using 717 [ 18 F ] [^{18}\mathrm{F}] FDG PET/CT scans for downstream segmentation of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) [ 19 ] . Collectively, these studies demonstrate the potential of self-supervised pretraining to alleviate annotation scarcity in whole-body PET/CT imaging. However, current self-supervised pretraining approaches remain limited in the scale and diversity of pretraining data, cross-modal interaction modeling, breadth and clinical comprehensiveness of downstream evaluation as detailed below.
blocks.zh: 自我监督的预训提供了一个统一的替代方案,利用大量无标签的PET/CT扫描来学习域特异性表现,通过微调可以适应分解,或者用作损伤分类的特征提取器. 近年来,一些研究探讨了全身PET/CT损伤分析的自我监督预训[46、30、15、19、24]。 亚兹达尼等. 自我监督 SwinUNETR预训使用752个全身 [68 Ga] [^{-68}\-mathrm{Ga}]-PSMA-11 PET/CT扫描前列腺癌元质分解,并演示了预训对下游损伤分解的好处 [46]. Oh等人利用从可公开获取的AutoPET III数据集取出1,292个样本,应用了以对比性学习为基础的预训,并评价了其对损害分解和对私营机构群体进行分类的好处[30]。 黄等. 采用AutoPET III的507个FDG案例,提出了学习跨模式的PET/CT表述模式补充掩码策略[15]. 刘等. 对FDG重点基础模型采用类似方式补充口罩,在4,997个扫描器上预先训练[24]. 凯沙瓦尔兹等. 采用多式联运 SwinUNETR 预训使用 717 [18 F] [^{18}\ mathrm{F}] FDG PET/CT扫描下游分解散出大B细胞淋巴瘤(DLBCL)[19]. 这些研究集体表明,自我监督的预训有可能缓解全身PET/CT成像中注意不足的情况。 然而,如下文所详述的,在培训前数据的规模和多样性、跨模式互动模式、广度和下游评价临床全面性方面,目前自我监督的预培训方法仍然有限。

blocks.en: 1. Limited pretraining scale and tracer diversity: A major advantage of self-supervised learning is its ability to exploit large and heterogeneous pools of unlabeled data. However, several existing PET/CT pretraining studies have been conducted using relatively modest cohorts, including 752, 1,292, 507, and 717 scans in [ 46 , 30 , 15 , 19 ] , respectively. In addition to the limited scale, most existing approaches are developed using a single tracer, with FDG-based cohorts used in [ 15 , 24 , 19 ] and PSMA-based data used in [ 46 ] . Although Oh et al. incorporated data with greater tracer diversity [ 30 ] , dataset size was modest (1,292) limiting diverse feature learning, and systematic evaluation across FDG and PSMA tracers were not explored. Together, the limited cohort size and tracer diversity may constrain the ability of self-supervised pretraining to capture the full spectrum of anatomical, pathological, image acquisition related, and tracer-specific and tracer-agnostic variations encountered in clinical PET/CT imaging. As new radiotracers are being developed and used for different clinical applications, such limited training and tracer-specific models may not yield generalizable representations that are tracer-adaptable. Larger and more heterogeneous multi-institution, multi-tracer cohorts are therefore needed to develop more robust and transferable PET/CT representations. 2. Limited cross-modal interaction modeling: PET and CT provide complementary information, with PET capturing molecular and physiological activity and CT providing anatomical and structural context. Features in both modalities also vary based on the anatomical region in whole-body and whether the region contains cancer or not. Clinicians use these imaging features on both modalities during interpretation, but, most existing pretraining approaches do not explicitly learn these relationships between PET and CT images. Yazdani et al. [ 46 ] , for example, followed the original SwinUNETR pretraining proxy tasks, including image rotation prediction, image volume inpainting, and contrastive coding [ 11 ] , while Keshavarz et al. adopted a conventional masked-reconstruction strategy without explicitly modeling modality-specific interactions. More recent approaches [ 30 , 15 , 24 ] introduce modality-complementary masking, in which one modality is masked while the complementary modality remains available. Although this strategy encourages cross-modal information learning, its robustness under modality corruption, imaging noise, and distribution shifts remains insufficiently characterized. 3. Narrow and clinically limited downstream evaluation: A robust pretrained representation should transfer across multiple clinically relevant tasks and remain reliable under heterogeneous and potentially degraded imaging conditions (e.g., poor image quality, artifacts, PET-CT misalignment due to patient movement, or missing modality). However, the majority of existing PET/CT self-supervised pretraining studies assess their representations primarily through lesion segmentation [ 46 , 15 , 19 , 24 ] . Oh et al. additionally evaluate staging classification [ 30 ] , but lesion-level classification tasks, such as distinguishing malignant from normal patches, remain comparatively underexplored. Such region-level classification is clinically important in triage settings for flagging if a patient has cancer in a specific region or in the whole body, that may warrant more detailed investigation. Moreover, segmentation performance is commonly evaluated using voxel-level metrics such as Dice score, intersection-over-union (IoU), and Hausdorff distance. While these measures quantify spatial overlap, they do not fully capture clinically meaningful performance for staging, treatment planning, and response assessment, such as whether and how many individual lesions are correctly detected or missed, and whether specific anatomic regions contain cancer. Lesion-level sensitivity, specificity, precision, false-positive burden, and anatomical-region-specific performance therefore provide important clinically-relevant information. Last but not the least, performance robustness under likely PET/CT image quality issues, including image noise, missing modality and PET/CT misalignment has received limited attention, despite being essential for assessing model reliability under real-world acquisition variability. A comprehensive evaluation of pretrained representations should therefore span multiple downstream tasks, clinically relevant lesion-level metrics, anatomically stratified analysis, and robustness testing under realistic imaging perturbations.

blocks.en: Limited pretraining scale and tracer diversity: A major advantage of self-supervised learning is its ability to exploit large and heterogeneous pools of unlabeled data. However, several existing PET/CT pretraining studies have been conducted using relatively modest cohorts, including 752, 1,292, 507, and 717 scans in [ 46 , 30 , 15 , 19 ] , respectively. In addition to the limited scale, most existing approaches are developed using a single tracer, with FDG-based cohorts used in [ 15 , 24 , 19 ] and PSMA-based data used in [ 46 ] . Although Oh et al. incorporated data with greater tracer diversity [ 30 ] , dataset size was modest (1,292) limiting diverse feature learning, and systematic evaluation across FDG and PSMA tracers were not explored. Together, the limited cohort size and tracer diversity may constrain the ability of self-supervised pretraining to capture the full spectrum of anatomical, pathological, image acquisition related, and tracer-specific and tracer-agnostic variations encountered in clinical PET/CT imaging. As new radiotracers are being developed and used for different clinical applications, such limited training and tracer-specific models may not yield generalizable representations that are tracer-adaptable. Larger and more heterogeneous multi-institution, multi-tracer cohorts are therefore needed to develop more robust and transferable PET/CT representations.

blocks.en: Limited cross-modal interaction modeling: PET and CT provide complementary information, with PET capturing molecular and physiological activity and CT providing anatomical and structural context. Features in both modalities also vary based on the anatomical region in whole-body and whether the region contains cancer or not. Clinicians use these imaging features on both modalities during interpretation, but, most existing pretraining approaches do not explicitly learn these relationships between PET and CT images. Yazdani et al. [ 46 ] , for example, followed the original SwinUNETR pretraining proxy tasks, including image rotation prediction, image volume inpainting, and contrastive coding [ 11 ] , while Keshavarz et al. adopted a conventional masked-reconstruction strategy without explicitly modeling modality-specific interactions. More recent approaches [ 30 , 15 , 24 ] introduce modality-complementary masking, in which one modality is masked while the complementary modality remains available. Although this strategy encourages cross-modal information learning, its robustness under modality corruption, imaging noise, and distribution shifts remains insufficiently characterized.

blocks.en: Narrow and clinically limited downstream evaluation: A robust pretrained representation should transfer across multiple clinically relevant tasks and remain reliable under heterogeneous and potentially degraded imaging conditions (e.g., poor image quality, artifacts, PET-CT misalignment due to patient movement, or missing modality). However, the majority of existing PET/CT self-supervised pretraining studies assess their representations primarily through lesion segmentation [ 46 , 15 , 19 , 24 ] . Oh et al. additionally evaluate staging classification [ 30 ] , but lesion-level classification tasks, such as distinguishing malignant from normal patches, remain comparatively underexplored. Such region-level classification is clinically important in triage settings for flagging if a patient has cancer in a specific region or in the whole body, that may warrant more detailed investigation. Moreover, segmentation performance is commonly evaluated using voxel-level metrics such as Dice score, intersection-over-union (IoU), and Hausdorff distance. While these measures quantify spatial overlap, they do not fully capture clinically meaningful performance for staging, treatment planning, and response assessment, such as whether and how many individual lesions are correctly detected or missed, and whether specific anatomic regions contain cancer. Lesion-level sensitivity, specificity, precision, false-positive burden, and anatomical-region-specific performance therefore provide important clinically-relevant information. blocks.en: In this work, we address the above limitations of existing self-supervised pretraining approaches for whole-body PET/CT by developing and validating a novel, multimodal self-supervised learning method with context-aware joint unimodal reconstruction and cross-modal translation. Our method, Lost or Replaced Masked Image Modeling (LoRe-MIM), explicitly learns PET–CT relationships, unimodal structural consistency and anatomy from a large-scale, multi-tracer, multi-institutional pretraining cohort. We evaluate the learned representations through comprehensive downstream evaluation across segmentation and classification tasks. In addition to conventional predictive performance, we evaluate clinically relevant lesion-level performance and robustness under clinically-relevant imaging perturbations. Our main contributions are summarized as follows:
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们通过开发并验证一种新颖的、多式的、自我监督的学习方法,同时采用具有环境意识的联合单一模式重建和跨模式翻译,解决了现有全体PET/CT自我监督的预培训方法的上述局限性。 我们的方法,即丢失或被替换的蒙面图像模型(LoRe-MIM),从大规模、多轨、多机构预训群体中明确学习PET-CT关系、单模式结构一致性和解剖学。 我们通过分门别类和分类任务的综合下游评价来评价所学到的表述。 除了传统的预测性能外,我们还在临床相关的成像扰动下,评价临床相关的损伤级性能和稳健性. 我们的主要贡献概述如下:

blocks.en: 1. Large and heterogeneous PET/CT cohort: We combine publicly available datasets, including AutoPET-III ( N = 1,611 N=1,611 ), SPADE ( N = 1,126 N=1,126 ), ViMED ( N = 1,995 N=1,995 ), and Deep-PSMA ( N = 200 N=200 ), with an institutional cohort from Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center (DHMC; N = 1,599 N=1,599 ), yielding a total of 6,531 whole-body PET/CT scans, of which 5,910 are used for self-supervised pretraining and 621 for evaluation. The cohort spans multiple cancer types, including melanoma, lung cancer, lymphoma, and prostate cancer, as well as multiple PET tracers, including FDG and PSMA. This large-scale collection captures substantial real-world heterogeneity in patient populations, disease distributions, scanners, institutions, acquisition settings, and tracer characteristics, providing a diverse foundation for learning transferable PET/CT representations. 2. Lost or Replaced Masked Image Modeling (LoRe-MIM): We introduce a novel multimodal masked image modeling strategy called Lost or Replaced Masked Image Modelling (LoRe-MIM) that mimics a situation of solving two jumbled-up puzzles, with some puzzle pieces that are ‘lost’ and some pieces are ‘replaced’ with a corresponding piece from the other puzzle. Rather than relying solely on conventional masking [ 19 ] or keeping one modality fully intact while masking the other [ 15 , 24 ] , our approach combines standard zero-mean masking with cross-modal replacement of spatially corresponding PET and CT blocks. During cross-modal replacement, a corrupted block from one modality is replaced by the co-located content from the complementary modality while the reconstruction target remains the original block. This hybrid objective encourages the model to jointly learn intra-modality contextual structure through the zero-mean masking, and bidirectional PET ↔ \leftrightarrow CT correspondences through the context-aware translation within a unified self-supervised framework. 3. Extensive clinically relevant downstream evaluation: We evaluate the learned representations through a variety of clinically-relevant downstream tasks including (a) whole-body multimodal image reconstruction, (b) patch-level classification into cancer vs non-cancer, (c) robustness evaluation with patch-based classification, (d) whole-body lesion segmentation, and (e) label-efficient segmentation training. We evaluate whole body reconstruction performance for both PET and CT images to assess how well the model learns modality-specific anatomic features as well as PET-CT relationships. For patch-based classification tasks, we assess performance with clean as well as degraded imaging conditions to evaluate robustness. For lesion segmentation, beyond conventional voxel-level segmentation metrics, we report clinically relevant lesion-level performance and stratified results across anatomical regions, PET tracers, different cancer types, and different multi-institutional datasets.

blocks.zh: 广泛的临床相关下游评价: 我们通过各种与临床相关的下游任务,包括(a) 全身多模式图像重建,(b) 将补丁级分类为癌症与非癌症,(c) 以补丁级分类进行强健性评价,(d) 全身损伤分解,(e) 标签效率高的分解培训,来评价学到的表述。 我们评价PET和CT图像的整体身体重建性能,以评估模型如何很好地学习特定模式的原子特征以及PET-CT关系. 对于以补丁为基础的分类任务,我们以清洁和退化的成像条件评估性能,以评价稳健性。 对于损伤分解,除了常规的活性分解度测量标准外,我们报告临床上相关的损伤分解水平性能和分层结果,包括解剖区、PET示踪器、不同的癌症类型和不同的多机构数据集。

blocks.en: Our experiments demonstrate that pretraining with large-scale, multi-tracer, pan-cancer heterogeneous PET/CT datasets improves lesion segmentation, label-efficient training, classification, robustness to image quality degradation and reconstruction. Our proposed LoRE-MIM improves performance across all downstream tasks over conventional MAE-style and cross-modal masking baselines, providing generalizable, tracer-adaptable representations that can be used for different PET/CT tasks, cancers and PET tracers.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验表明,使用大规模、多致癌、多发性、泛癌的多种PET/CT数据集进行预训可改善损伤分解、标签效率高的培训、分类、图像质量退化和重建。 我们提议的LORE-MIM比常规的MAE型和跨模式遮掩基线提高了所有下游任务的性能,提供了可通用的可跟踪的表达,可用于不同的PET/CT任务,癌症和PET跟踪.

blocks.en: In this work, we aim to learn latent representations from whole-body PET/CT scans through self-supervised pretraining of an encoder–decoder architecture. Specifically, we adopt the Masked Image Modeling (MIM) paradigm for 3D medical imaging, in which paired and spatially aligned 3D patches are extracted from whole-body PET/CT scans and perturbed using a masking strategy. blocks.en: 2.5 Evaluation of LoRE-MIM Pretraining
blocks.zh: 2.5 评价LORE-MIM预训

blocks.en: We conduct several experiments to test if our self-supervised pretraining method enables learning robust features for improving whole-body reconstruction, distinguishing cancereous tissue from normal tissue via classification and lesion segmentation tasks, is robust to noise, missing modality, and PET/CT misalignment, and enables label-efficient training. We also test whether our method is generalizable across tracers and multi-institutional data.
blocks.zh: 我们进行了几次实验,测试我们自我监督的预训方法是否能够学习强健的特征,改善全身重建,通过分类和损伤分解任务将癌症组织与正常组织区分开来,强于噪音,缺失模式,以及PET/CT错配,并使得标签效率高的培训得以进行. 我们还测试我们的方法是否可以在追踪器和多机构数据中通用。

blocks.en: 2.5.1 Whole-body multimodal image reconstruction
blocks.zh: 2.5.1 国家 全体多模式图像重建

blocks.en: We first evaluate the reconstruction capability of our self-supervised 3D patch-based pretraining model on whole-body multimodal PET/CT images. We employ a sliding-window inference strategy with a patch size of 96 × 128 × 128 96\times 128\times 128 voxels to reconstruct the entire volume. Overlapping reconstructed patches are subsequently aggregated using Gaussian-weighted averaging to minimize boundary artifacts and ensure spatial continuity in the reconstructed whole-body PET/CT images.
blocks.zh: 我们首先评估我们自我监督的基于3D补丁的预训模型在全身多模式PET/CT图像上的重建能力. 我们采用滑窗推论策略,修补尺寸为96×128×12896\times128\times128voxels来重建整个音量. 相重叠的重建补丁随后被用高斯加权平均值来进行聚合,以尽量减少边界文物,并确保重建后全身PET/CT图像的空间连续性.

blocks.en: The reconstructed whole-body volumes are evaluated using three metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Structural Similarity Index (SSIM), and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR). MAE quantifies the average absolute voxel-wise difference between the original and reconstructed scans. SSIM measures the structural similarity between the original and reconstructed 3D volumes, while PSNR assesses reconstruction fidelity relative to the maximum signal intensity. Overall, lower MAE and higher SSIM and PSNR values indicate better reconstruction performance.
blocks.zh: 采用三个标准来评价重建后的全身体积: 平均绝对出错(MAE),结构相似性指数(SSIM)和峰相信号对噪比(PSNR). MAE将原始扫描与重建扫描之间的平均绝对阴道相差进行量化. SSIM测量出原作与重建的3D卷的结构相似性,而PSNR则根据最大信号强度来评估重建的忠实性. 总体来说,低低的MAE值和高的SSIM值和PSNR值表明重建绩效较好.

blocks.en: 2.5.3 Robustness evaluation with patch-based classification
blocks.zh: 2.5.3 有补丁分类的强性评价

blocks.en: We evaluate the robustness of the learned representations for patch classification using synthetically perturbed 3D PET/CT patches under three clinically relevant scenarios: (1) noisy images, (2) spatial misalignment between PET and CT modalities due to registration errors, and (3) missing modality information, where either PET or CT is unavailable. • Robustness to Noisy Images: We independently introduce zero-mean Gaussian noise into PET and CT patches of testing cohort to evaluate the robustness of the learned representations to image corruption. These perturbations provide a controlled approximation of image quality degradation that may arise from variations in image acquisition and reconstruction. Specifically, Gaussian noise is independently added to the PET and CT voxels, with standard deviations set to 0.1 times the corresponding modality’s intensity standard deviation computed from the clean training data. The resulting corrupted intensities are clipped to the intensity range of the corresponding modality in the clean training data. • Robustness to PET/CT misalignment: Spatial misalignment between PET and CT may arise from patient movement between acquisitions [ 47 ] , differences in respiratory states [ 4 ] , and artifacts introduced by CT-based attenuation correction in the presence of respiratory motion [ 31 ] . We simulate such spatial misalignment between PET and CT modalities by applying random geometric transformations to the CT channel of each test patch while keeping the PET channel unchanged. Specifically, we independently sample in-plane rotations about the z z -axis uniformly from [ − 5 ∘ , 5 ∘ ] [-5^{\circ},5^{\circ}] and translations along the x x - and y y -axes uniformly from [ − 2 , 2 ] [-2,2] voxels, while maintaining zero translation along the z z -axis. The transformed CT patches are resampled using trilinear interpolation with zero padding. These perturbations simulate registration errors between PET and CT modalities while preserving both modalities. • Robustness to Missing Modality: We simulate scenarios in which either the PET or CT modality is unavailable to evaluate the robustness of the learned representations to missing modality information. Specifically, we consider two scenarios: (1) Missing-PET, where all PET voxel intensities are set to zero while the CT channel remains unchanged, and (2) Missing-CT, where all CT voxel intensities are set to zero while the PET channel remains unchanged.

blocks.en: We adopt voxel-level, lesion-level, and anatomical region-level evaluation metrics as below:
blocks.zh: 我们采用以下阴道、损伤和解剖区域一级的评价指标:

blocks.en: 1. Voxel-level Evaluation: Following Rokuss et al. [ 32 ] , we use the Dice similarity coefficient, false-positive volume (FPVol), and false-negative volume (FNVol) as voxel-level evaluation metrics. Dice quantifies the spatial overlap between the predicted and ground truth segmentations. FPVol measures the total volume of tissue incorrectly predicted as lesions, whereas FNVol measures the total volume of ground truth lesion tissue missed by the model. We report these metrics only for diseased cases. 2. Lesion-level Evaluation: We identify individual lesions in the predicted and ground truth segmentation masks using morphological processing and connected component analysis. We then aggregate lesion-level counts across all test patients and compute sensitivity, defined as the proportion of ground truth lesions detected, and positive predictive value (PPV), defined as the proportion of predicted lesions that match ground truth lesions. 3. Anatomical Region-level Evaluation: Treatment decisions are often influenced by the presence of metastases in specific anatomical sites, such as the liver or bones. We therefore evaluate segmentation performance in four anatomical regions: the liver, lungs, bones, and high-risk bones. We use TotalSegmentator [ 42 ] to obtain anatomical masks and compute region-level Dice, FPVol, and FNVol using the voxel-level definitions restricted to each region. We also compute region-level sensitivity, defined as the proportion of ground truth lesion-containing regions in which at least one lesion is correctly detected, and specificity, defined as the proportion of ground truth lesion-free regions in which no lesion is predicted. 2.5.5 Label-Efficient Segmentation Training Obtaining voxel-wise annotations for whole-body lesion segmentation is a time-consuming and resource-intensive process that requires substantial clinical expertise. As discussed in Sect. 1 , the growing volume of whole-body PET/CT examinations further widens the gap between imaging demand and the availability of expert radiologists to generate or verify such annotations. Therefore, we evaluate the effectiveness of self-supervised pretraining under label-efficient finetuning settings by utilizing varying proportions (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%, 50%, and 100%) of the labeled training data for whole-body lesion segmentation. Evaluation Method: We evaluate segmentation performance using Dice and report the results across all evaluated percentages of labeled training data.

For each fine-tuning variant described in Sect. 2.5.4 , we initialize the frozen network components with their corresponding pretrained weights from the pretraining phase, while the remaining trainable parameters are randomly initialized and optimized during fine-tuning.

blocks.en: 3 Ablation Studies for Pretraining Approaches
blocks.zh: 3 预训方法的关系研究

blocks.en: 3.1 Masking Strategies
blocks.zh: 3.1 蒙面战略

blocks.en: We conduct an ablation study examining three special cases of the proposed Lost-or-Replaced (LoRe) masking framework to investigate the contributions of different masking strategies to self-supervised representation learning. A Lost perturbation sets the selected block to zero, whereas a Replaced perturbation substitutes the spatially corresponding block from the other modality. Based on this formulation, we consider three masking variants:

This strategy evaluates representation learning when only one modality is perturbed. 2. Lost-Both MIM (LB-MIM): We apply the same zero-masking pattern to both modalities by sampling a shared mask m ( b ) ∼ Bernoulli ⁡ ( 0.5 ) m^{(b)}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(0.5) and setting m PET ( b ) = m CT ( b ) = m ( b ) m_{\mathrm{PET}}^{(b)}=m_{\mathrm{CT}}^{(b)}=m^{(b)} and z PET ( b ) = z CT ( b ) = 1 z_{\mathrm{PET}}^{(b)}=z_{\mathrm{CT}}^{(b)}=1 . Thus, spatially corresponding PET and CT blocks are simultaneously set to zero, removing direct input information from both modalities at the selected locations. 3. Replaced-MIM (Re-MIM): We apply only cross-modal replacement by setting z PET ( b ) = z CT ( b ) = 0 z_{\mathrm{PET}}^{(b)}=z_{\mathrm{CT}}^{(b)}=0 and independently sampling m PET ( b ) , m CT ( b ) ∼ Bernoulli ⁡ ( 0.5 ) m_{\mathrm{PET}}^{(b)},m_{\mathrm{CT}}^{(b)}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(0.5) . Each selected PET block is replaced with the corresponding original CT block, and each selected CT block is replaced with the corresponding original PET block. This strategy isolates the contribution of cross-modal replacement without introducing zero masking.

blocks.en: 3.2 Augmentation
blocks.zh: 3.2 增加额

blocks.en: We investigate the impact of data augmentation during self-supervised pretraining on reconstruction and patch classification (cancer vs. non-cancer) performance. We adopt the whole-body PET/CT-specific augmentation strategies employed by Rokuss et al. [ 32 ] , incorporating both spatial and intensity-based transformations. Spatial augmentations include random rotations, scaling, and mirroring, while intensity-based augmentations include Gaussian noise, Gaussian blurring, brightness scaling, contrast adjustment, and gamma correction. Additionally, we simulate reduced image resolution and spatial misalignment between PET and CT modalities to account for variations in image quality and intermodal registration.
blocks.zh: 我们调查在自行监督的重建预训和补丁分类(癌症与非癌症)表现过程中数据增强的影响. 我们采用Rokus等人采用的全体PET/CT专用增强战略。 [32],既包括空间变换,也包括强度变换. 空间增强包括随机自转,缩放,和反射等,而以强度为基础的增强包括高斯噪音,高斯模糊,亮度缩放,对比度调整,和伽马校正等. 此外,我们模拟PET和CT模式之间的图像分辨率降低和空间错配,以考虑到图像质量和多联登记的变化。

blocks.zh: 3.3 可变面具

blocks.en:
We investigate the effect of masking variable portions of each modality in both Re-MIM and LoRe-MIM pretraining.
For each sampled training patch of 96 × 128 × 128 96\times 128\times 128 voxels, the CT and

Randomly selected, non-overlapping blocks of 12 × 16 × 16 12\times 16\times 16 voxels are masked according to the sampled ratio for each modality, with new ratios and mask locations sampled whenever a training patch was drawn.
Both the ablation masking strategy (Re-MIM and LoRe-MIM) retains its original replacement strategy. We evaluated variable masking alone and in combination with augmentation. Validation used no augmentation and a fixed masking ratio of 0.5 0.5 for
each modality.

blocks.zh: 4 比较基准模型

blocks.en: 4.1 Reconstruction
blocks.zh: 4.1 重建

blocks.en: We compare our proposed LoRe-MIM with an off-the-shelf whole-body self-supervised model trained with FDG PET/CT, released by Liu et al. [ 24 ] . We denote this baseline as FDG-only MAE .

blocks.en: 4.2 Segmentation Models
blocks.zh: 4.2 分块模型

blocks.en: We consider two baseline models for comparison with our finetuned segmentation models: (1) SwinUNETR trained from scratch and (2) the whole-body PET/CT-based nnU-Net architecture proposed by [ 32 ] , also trained from scratch. For fair comparison, we utilize the same preprocessed samples, same training framework released by [ 32 ] with similar augmenttaion and same number of training epochs.

blocks.en: 4.3 Classification performance with pretrained features
blocks.zh: 4.3 具有预训特征的分类性能

blocks.en:
We compare our pretrained representations with those extracted from DINOv3 [ 36 ] and ResNet50-3D [ 6 ] . For both baselines, PET and CT patches are independently normalized using their respective means and standard deviations (with a minimum standard deviation of 10 − 6 10^{-6} ) and concatenated side by side.
For ResNet50-3D, global average pooling of the final feature map produces a 2048-dimensional feature vector. For DINOv3, each axial slice is resized to 224 × 224 224\times 224 , replicated across three channels, and processed independently. The resulting slice-level features are averaged to obtain a single feature vector per patch.

blocks.en: 5.2.2 Patch-level classification into cancer vs non-cancer
blocks.zh: 5.2.2 补丁级癌症与非癌症的分类

blocks.en: We first evaluate patch-based classification performance on the clean AutoPET-III test set using features extracted from the SwinUNETR encoder. For all comparisons, we employ logistic regression (LR) for classification using the extracted features, with dimensionality reduction applied where specified. As shown in Table 5 , encoder features aggregated using global average pooling (GAP) achieve a higher AUC with PCA using 384 components (0.7180) than with 128 components (0.6974). Furthermore, GAP generally outperforms feature flattening, highlighting the benefits of spatial feature aggregation. We also note that linear dimensionality reduction with PCA outperforms non-linear KPCA for 128 and 384 feature dimensions, suggesting that learned representations have good linear separability in cancer vs non-cancer patterns. We then investigate features extracted from different decoder stages and observe that decoder representations consistently outperform encoder representations. In particular, Dec 4 achieves the highest AUC (0.7790), surpassing both DINOv3 (0.7589) and ResNet50-3D (0.7120). These results highlight the effectiveness of intermediate decoder representations learned through LoRe-MIM pretraining for downstream patch-based classification.
blocks.zh: 我们首先利用从SwinUNETR编码器中提取的特性,在干净的AutoPET-III测试集上评价以补丁为基础的分类性能. 在所有比较中,我们使用逻辑回归法(LR)来利用所提取的特征进行分类,在具体情况下适用维度降低。 如表5所示,使用全球平均集合(GAP)汇总的编码器特性使PCA使用384个组件(0.7180)的AUC比128个组件(0.6974)的编码高。 此外,GAP一般表现优于平分,突出了空间地物聚合的好处。 我们还注意到,五氯苯甲醚的线性维度降低在128和384个特征维度上超过了非线性KPCA,这表明所学表现在癌症与非癌症模式中具有良好的线性分离性。 然后,我们调查从不同的解码器阶段提取的特征,并观察到解码器的表示一直优于编码器的表示. 特别是,Dec 4实现了最高的AUC(0.7790),同时超过了DINOv3(0.7589)和ResNet50-3D(0.7120). 这些结果凸显出通过LoRe-MIM预训为下游补丁分类所学到的中间解码器表达的效果.

blocks.en: 5.2.3 Robustness evaluation with patch-based classification
blocks.zh: 5.2.3 有补丁分类的强性评价

blocks.en: Table 6 presents the robustness evaluation of patch-based classification using features extracted from the fourth decoder stage (Dec 4 ) of our LoRe-MIM pretrained SwinUNETR under perturbed 3D PET/CT inputs. Our pretrained decoder features consistently outperform the ResNet50-3D and DINOv3 baselines across all four perturbation settings. Under Gaussian noise, our method achieves an AUC of 0.7584, compared with 0.7555 for DINOv3 and 0.7268 for ResNet50-3D. Similarly, under simulated PET/CT misalignment, our method achieves a higher AUC (0.7648) than DINOv3 (0.7286) and ResNet50-3D (0.7332). More notably, all methods exhibit substantial performance degradation when either imaging modality is missing, with missing PET resulting in considerably lower AUC than missing CT. Nevertheless, our method maintains an AUC of 0.6975 under missing CT and 0.5995 under missing PET, outperforming DINOv3 (0.6500 and 0.5344) and ResNet50-3D (0.6217 and 0.5348), respectively. The largest performance gap between our method and DINOv3 occurs when PET is missing (0.0651 AUC), suggesting that our learned representations are less sensitive to the absence of PET information. These findings support the potential of LoRe-MIM to capture complementary cross-modal representations and improve classification robustness under incomplete or corrupted PET/CT inputs.

blocks.en: 5.2.4 Whole-body lesion segmentation with test-set
blocks.zh: 5.2.4 (中文(简体) ). 带有试验装置的全身损伤分解

blocks.en: We use 321 321 cases from AutoPET-III and 200 200 cases from Deep-PSMA as independent test sets for whole-body lesion segmentation. These cases are strictly excluded from both the pretraining and finetuning stages, ensuring no overlap with the training or validation cohorts used in either stage.
blocks.zh: 我们使用AutoPET-III的321 321个病例和Deep-PSMA的200个病例作为全身损伤分解的独立测试集. 这些案件严格排除在预训和微调阶段之外,确保不会与两个阶段使用的培训或鉴定组重叠。

blocks.en: We compare our proposed LoRe-MIM pretrained SwinUNETR against SwinUNETR and nnU-Net trained from scratch, considering three finetuning configurations: Full FT, Dec. FT, and Enc. + Dec. FT, as described in Sect. 2.5.4 . Among these configurations, Enc. + Dec. FT achieves the highest Dice scores (0.581 and 0.613) and lesion sensitivities (0.776 and 0.759) on AutoPET-III and Deep-PSMA, respectively. Compared with SwinUNETR trained from scratch, these correspond to relative Dice improvements of 10.5% and 12.1%, respectively (Table 7 ). However, the optimal finetuning configuration varies across evaluation metrics. On AutoPET-III, Full FT achieves the lowest FPVol (15.594 cc), while Dec. FT achieves the lowest FNVol (7.405 cc). On Deep-PSMA, Dec. FT achieves the lowest FPVol (48.432 cc) and FNVol (6.588 cc). Despite these improvements, nnU-Net trained from scratch achieves the highest lesion-level PPV on both AutoPET-III (0.733) and Deep-PSMA (0.768), indicating a trade-off between lesion detection sensitivity and precision. We further present tracer-stratified Dice, FPVol, and FNVol in Figures 2 and 3 . For PSMA scans in AutoPET-III, Enc. + Dec. FT achieves the lowest FPVol (17.68 cc), whereas Dec. FT achieves the lowest FNVol (7.15 cc). In contrast, for PSMA scans in Deep-PSMA, Dec. FT achieves the lowest FPVol (57.73 cc), while Full FT achieves the lowest FNVol (4.90 cc). Overall, these results demonstrate that LoRe-MIM pretraining improves segmentation overlap across both datasets, while different finetuning configurations exhibit distinct trade-offs between false-positive and false-negative predictions.

blocks.en: Figures 4 and 5 present anatomical-region-level segmentation performance across four regions (liver, lung, bone, and HR-bone) on AutoPET-III and Deep-PSMA, respectively, evaluated using Dice, FPVol, FNVol, lesion sensitivity, and specificity, computed for each region independently. Across both datasets, the best-performing LoRe-MIM finetuning variants consistently improve Dice over SwinUNETR trained from scratch in all four anatomical regions, with the largest improvements observed in the liver. Specifically, liver Dice increases from 0.36 to 0.48 on AutoPET-III and from 0.25 to 0.42 on Deep-PSMA, corresponding to relative improvements of 33.3% and 68.0%, respectively. Improvements are also observed in the lung (0.44 to 0.49 and 0.42 to 0.48), bone (0.53 to 0.57 and 0.64 to 0.67), and HR-bone (0.55 to 0.60 and 0.66 to 0.68) on AutoPET-III and Deep-PSMA, respectively. In addition to improved segmentation overlap, LoRe-MIM enhances lesion-level specificity in bone and HR-bone regions. On AutoPET-III, bone specificity increases from 0.72 to 0.85, while on Deep-PSMA, HR-bone specificity increases from 0.67 to 0.87 compared with SwinUNETR trained from scratch. For liver lesions, all three LoRe-MIM finetuning variants achieve higher sensitivity (0.85–0.92) than SwinUNETR trained from scratch (0.73) on Deep-PSMA, whereas liver sensitivity remains consistently high (1.00) across all configurations on AutoPET-III. Interestingly, improvements in liver Dice exhibit contrasting FPVol–FNVol trade-offs across the two datasets. On AutoPET-III, Enc. + Dec. FT reduces liver FPVol from 3.74 to 2.03 cc compared with SwinUNETR Scratch, accompanied by a slight increase in FNVol from 3.43 to 3.57 cc. Conversely, on Deep-PSMA, Dec. FT reduces liver FNVol from 4.53 to 2.74 cc while increasing FPVol from 7.77 to 21.31 cc. These findings suggest that LoRe-MIM improves anatomical-region-level segmentation across both datasets, although the relative contributions of reduced false-positive and false-negative volumes vary with the dataset and finetuning configuration.

blocks.en: 6 Discussion
blocks.zh: 讨论

blocks.en: In this work, we aim to bridge the research gap arising from label scarcity in developing deep learning models for whole-body lesion segmentation and patch-based classification using PET/CT scans. To address this challenge, we seek to leverage well-established self-supervised pretraining schemes to learn rich and transferable representations of whole-body PET/CT scans. Existing pretraining approaches in the whole-body PET/CT domain often rely on relatively small cohorts, incorporate limited cross-modal interactions, and primarily evaluate the effectiveness of pretraining through downstream segmentation tasks only. In this work, we aim to address these limitations through a large-scale, heterogeneous pretraining dataset, a novel cross-modal masked image modeling strategy, and an extensive evaluation across multiple downstream tasks.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们的目标是在利用PET/CT扫描为全身损伤分解和补丁分类开发深层学习模型时,弥补标签稀缺造成的研究差距。 为了应对这一挑战,我们力求利用完善的自我监督的预训计划,学习全体PET/CT扫描的丰富和可转移的表述。 整个机构PET/CT领域的现有预训方法往往依赖相对较少的组群,包含有限的跨模式互动,主要通过下游分流任务评价预训的有效性. 在这项工作中,我们的目标是通过大规模、多样化的预训数据集、新的跨模式遮掩图像模型制作战略以及跨下游多个任务的广泛评价来解决这些局限性。

blocks.en: First, we introduce one of the largest cohorts for PET/CT pretraining, comprising 5910 5910 unlabeled scans collected from both publicly available and institutional datasets (Sect. 2.1 ). In contrast to most prior pretraining cohorts that are either only FDG- or PSMA-specific, our dataset incorporates pan-cancer, multi-tracer PET/CT scans spanning diverse patient populations and scanner variations. Such heterogeneity enables the pretraining framework to learn more generalizable and robust representations across different imaging conditions and disease characteristics. We investigate the generalizability of the learned representations through whole-body lesion segmentation across independent testing cohorts, while evaluating their robustness through patch-based classification under clinically relevant perturbations.
blocks.zh: 首先,我们引进了PET/CT预训的最大组群之一,包括从公开的和机构数据集收集的5910 5910个无标签扫描(第2.1节)。 与以前大多数只针对FDG或PSMA的预训组群形成对照的是,我们的数据集包含了泛癌、多发性PET/CT扫描,覆盖不同的病人群体和扫描仪的变化。 这种异质性使预先训练框架能够了解不同成像条件和疾病特征中更加笼统和有力的表现。 我们通过在独立测试组群中进行全身损伤分解来调查所学表现的一般性,同时根据临床相关扰动通过补丁分类来评估其强性。

blocks.en: Second, we adopt a masked image modeling (MIM) based reconstruction objective, inspired by its success in natural images and medical imaging domains. However, the application of MIM in multimodal medical imaging remains relatively underexplored, and the few existing approaches often mimic unimodal masking strategies that capture relationships between spatially aligned imaging modalities and enable accurate prediction even when one modality is missing. This leaves considerable room for exploring cross-modal representation learning. To address this limitation, we propose LoRe-MIM , a novel masking strategy that emulates solving two puzzles simulataneously, in which some puzzle pieces from each puzzle are either lost or replaces with the alternate puzzle (Sect. 2.4 ). Instead of adopting a fixed strategy for either removing or replacing all the masked blocks, we randomize the perturbation process using a Bernoulli random variable with a probability of 0.5. Through this stochastic masking mechanism, we encourage the pretrained model to learn anatomy and within-modal structural consistency as well as cross-modal relationships, correlations and complementarity, thereby capturing richer representations of multimodal PET/CT scans. Through ablation studies, we demonstrate that our proposed LoRe-MIM achieves the best reconstruction performance across all three metrics (MAE, SSIM, and PSNR), along with the highest classification AUC, compared to alternative masking strategies.
blocks.zh: 第二,我们采用了一个基于蒙面图像模型(MIM)的重建目标,其灵感来自它在自然图像和医学成像领域的成功. 然而,MIM在多模式医疗成像中的应用仍然相对没有得到充分利用,现有的少数方法往往模仿单模式遮盖策略,这些策略捕捉出空间相通的成像模式之间的关系,即使在缺少一种模式时也能进行准确的预测. 这为探索跨模式的代表学习留下了相当大的空间。 为了解决这一局限,我们提议Lore-MIM,这是一种新式的掩盖策略,它模拟了两个谜题的迅速解决,其中每个谜题中的某些谜题要么丢失,要么取而代之(第2.4节)。 我们不采用固定策略去除或替换所有被遮盖的块,而是使用概率为0.5的伯努利随机变量随机地进行扰动过程. 通过这种有花样的遮盖机制,我们鼓励预先训练好的模型学习解剖学和模式内的结构一致性以及跨模式关系、相关性和互补性,从而捕捉到更丰富的多模式PET/CT扫描。 通过减税研究,我们表明,我们提议的LoRe-MIM在所有三个衡量标准(MAE、SSIM和PSNR)中都取得了最佳的重建业绩,以及最高的分类AUC,与替代的遮掩策略相比。

blocks.en: Third, we provide an extensive evaluation of our proposed dataset and pretraining strategy across multiple downstream tasks. While existing self-supervised pretraining approaches primarily evaluate their effectiveness through lesion segmentation, we investigate two complementary tasks: (1) patch-based classification and (2) whole-body lesion segmentation. We evaluate classification performance under both clean and perturbed imaging conditions, whereas segmentation performance is assessed at the voxel, lesion, and anatomical region levels.
blocks.zh: 第三,我们广泛评价我们提议的数据集和跨下游多个任务的培训前战略。 虽然现有的自我监督的预训方法主要通过损伤分解来评估其有效性,但我们调查了两个互补的任务:(1) 补丁分解和(2) 全身损伤分解. 我们评价在清洁和扰动成像条件下的分类性能,而分解性能则在阴道、损伤和解剖区域各级进行评估。

blocks.en: In patch-based classification, we systematically evaluate different feature extraction stages, feature aggregation strategies, and dimensionality reduction techniques. We observe that, among the evaluated configurations using encoder features, global average pooling (GAP) combined with logistic regression (LR) achieves the best classification performance. Interestingly, when adopting GAP and LR, features extracted from the decoder stages outperform those extracted from the encoder. Finally, using features extracted from the final decoder stage, we demonstrate that our pretrained representations achieve superior classification performance compared to widely adopted pretrained architectures, including DINOv3 and ResNet50-3D, under comparable feature dimensionality reduction settings.
blocks.zh: 在以补丁为基础的分类中,我们系统地评价不同特征提取阶段,特征聚合策略,和维度降低技术. 我们看到,在使用编码器特性评估的配置中,全球平均集合与物流回归(LR)相结合,实现了最好的分类性能。 有趣的是,在采用GAP和LR时,从解码器相中提取的特征超过了从编码器中提取的特征. 最后,我们利用从最终解码器阶段提取的特性,表明我们经过预先训练的表述,在类似特性维度降低设置下,与广泛采用的预先训练的架构(包括DINOv3和ResNet50-3D)相比,实现了优越的分类性能.

blocks.en: We also benchmark the robustness of our pretrained representations under clinically relevant perturbations. Specifically, we introduce Gaussian noise into the 3D PET/CT patches, emulate spatial misalignment between PET and CT, and simulate missing modalities by independently removing either CT or PET. Across these perturbation settings, we observe that features extracted from the final decoder stage consistently outperform those obtained from DINOv3 and ResNet50-3D. These findings further support our hypothesis that the heterogeneous pretraining dataset and proposed LoRe-MIM strategy facilitate the learning of robust representations that maintain discriminative performance even under degraded or incomplete imaging conditions. Notably, the superior performance compared to DINOv3 highlights the potential of domain-specific multimodal pretraining over widely adopted general-purpose foundation models for PET/CT-based analysis.
blocks.zh: 我们还根据与临床相关的扰动来衡量我们经过预先训练的表述是否有力。 具体来说,我们将高斯噪声引入到3D PET/CT补丁中,模仿PET和CT之间的空间错位,通过独立去除CT或PET来模拟缺失模式. 通过这些扰动设置,我们发现,从最后解码器阶段提取的特性一直比从DINOv3和ResNet50-3D获得的特性要好。 这些调查结果进一步支持我们的假设,即各种预先培训数据集和拟议的LoRe-MIM战略有助于学习即使在退化或不完整的成像条件下保持歧视性表现的有力表述。 值得注意的是,与DINOv3相比,优异的性能突出了特定领域多式联运预先培训相对于广泛采用的基于PET/CT的通用基础模型的潜力。

blocks.en: Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our pretraining approach for whole-body lesion segmentation. We investigate three different finetuning strategies by selectively finetuning different components of the pretrained model. Across all three strategies, for both of our testing datasets AutoPET-III and Deep-PSMA, we observe consistent improvements in Dice scores compared to the corresponding model trained from scratch, along with reductions in FPVol and FNVol in several configurations. Specifically, on AutoPET-III, finetuning both the encoder and decoder improves Dice from 0.526 to 0.581 and reduces FPVol from 27.147 cc to 15.662 cc, whereas on Deep-PSMA, decoder finetuning improves Dice from 0.547 to 0.610 while reducing FPVol from 74.315 cc to 48.432 cc and FNVol from 9.785 cc to 6.588 cc (Table 7 ). We further compare our approach with an independent nnU-Net architecture optimized for AutoPET-III, trained under comparable preprocessing, augmentation, and training conditions. Although our chosen architecture, SwinUNETR, trained from scratch performs inferiorly to nnU-Net, our pretraining strategy enables SwinUNETR to achieve improved segmentation performance and outperform the nnU-Net baseline in terms of Dice, achieving 0.581 compared to 0.566 on AutoPET-III and 0.613 compared to 0.561 on Deep-PSMA. Beyond voxel-level evaluation, we conduct comprehensive lesion-level and anatomical region-level analyses and observe that our pretraining approach improves lesion detection sensitivity and segmentation accuracy in clinically critical regions, particularly the liver and high-risk bone regions. These improvements highlight the potential clinical relevance of pretraining, especially for detecting and segmenting metastases in anatomically challenging and high-risk regions. Our label-efficiency curves in Figure 6 further demonstrate that the benefits of pretraining are most pronounced when only a limited number of labeled training samples are available, with diminishing gains as the number of labeled samples increases. The improvements in voxel- and lesion-level performance on the unseen Deep-PSMA dataset, which was not introduced during either pretraining or finetuning (Table 7 ), together with the anatomical region-level improvements (Figure 5 ) and label-efficiency gains (Figure 6 ), demonstrate the generalizability of the learned representations and highlight the effectiveness of our heterogeneous pretraining dataset and proposed perturbation strategy.
blocks.zh: 最后,我们展示了我们针对全身损伤分化的预训方法的有效性。 我们通过选择性地微调预训模型的不同组件来调查三种不同的微调策略. 在所有三项战略中,对于我们的测试数据集AutoPET-III和Deep-PSMA,我们观察到,与从零开始训练的相应模型相比,Dice分数的不断提高,以及FPVol和FNVol在几个配置中的减少。 具体来说,在AutoPET-III上,将编码器和解码器的微调从0.526改进为0.581,将FPVol从27.147 cc降低为15.662 cc,而Deep-PSMA上,解码器微调则改进了 剂量从0.547克降至0.610克,同时将FPVol从74.315克降至48.432克,FNVol从9.785克降至6.588克(表7)。 我们进一步将我们的方法与为AutoPET-III而优化的独立nU-Net架构进行比较,该架构在类似的预处理、增强和培训条件下得到培训。 虽然我们所选择的架构SwinUNETR从头到尾都表现得不如NNU-Net,但我们的预训战略使SwinUNETR能够实现更好的分化性能,并在Dice方面超越了NNU-Net的基准,实现了0.581,而AutoPET-III的0.566和Deep-PSMA的0.613和0.561。 除了病毒级评价外,我们还进行全面的损伤级和解剖级分析,并观察到我们的培训前方法提高了临床关键地区,特别是肝脏和高风险骨骼地区的损伤检测敏感性和分化精度。 这些改进突出了预先培训在临床上的潜在关联性,特别是在解剖方面具有挑战性和高风险的区域中检测和分化元数据。 我们的标签效率曲线在图6中进一步显示,在只有有限数量的标签培训样本的情况下,预训的好处最为明显,随着标签样本数量的增加,收益正在减少。 在未见的Deep-PSMA数据集上,阴道和损伤级性能的改进,无论是在预训或微调期间都没有采用(表7),加上解剖级的改进(图5)和标签效率的提高(图6),都表明了所学表现的通俗性,并突出了我们多种多样的预训数据集和拟议的扰动战略的有效性。

blocks.en: Overall, our findings demonstrate that the combination of a large-scale, heterogeneous PET/CT dataset and the proposed LoRe-MIM masking strategy enables effective learning of generalizable and robust multimodal representations. Through extensive evaluation of reconstruction, classification, robustness, and whole-body lesion segmentation, we show that the benefits of self-supervised pretraining extend beyond improvements in individual downstream tasks. In particular, our results highlight the importance of incorporating cross-modal interactions during pretraining and leveraging heterogeneous imaging cohorts to develop more reliable and transferable deep learning models for whole-body PET/CT analysis.
blocks.zh: 总体而言,我们的调查结果表明,将大规模、多样化的PET/CT数据集与拟议的LoRe-MIM遮掩战略结合起来,就能够有效学习通用而有力的多式联运表述。 通过对重建、分类、稳健性和全身损伤分化的广泛评价,我们表明,自我监督的预先训练的好处远远超出下游各项任务的改进。 特别是,我们的成果突出了在预先培训和利用不同成像组群时纳入跨模式互动的重要性,以开发更可靠和可转让的深层学习模型,用于全体PET/CT分析。

blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we introduced a novel self-supervised masked image modeling framework, LoRe-MIM , to learn generalizable and robust representations from whole-body PET/CT scans. We curated and subsequently leveraged a large-scale, heterogeneous pretraining cohort of 5,910 unlabeled PET/CT scans collected from both publicly available and institutional datasets. Our proposed block-based perturbation strategy encourages the learning of metabolic and complementary anatomical representations through a stochastic masking mechanism, in which image blocks are either removed (Lost) by replacing them with zero values or replaced (Replaced) with corresponding blocks from the alternate modality. We extensively evaluated our proposed framework across whole-body image reconstruction, patch-based classification of cancerous and non-cancerous regions, and whole-body lesion segmentation. We demonstrated that our method achieves superior reconstruction performance compared to an FDG-only pretrained model, improves classification performance under both clean and perturbed imaging conditions compared to established pretrained architectures such as DINOv3 and ResNet50-3D, and enhances lesion segmentation performance at the voxel, lesion, and anatomical region levels. Overall, these findings establish the utility of large-scale, heterogeneous pretraining datasets and the effectiveness of our proposed cross-modal self-supervised learning strategy in learning rich, generalizable, and robust representations for whole-body PET/CT analysis.
blocks.zh: 在这部作品中,我们引入了一个新的自我监督的蒙面图像模型框架"Lore-MIM",以从全身PET/CT扫描中学习通俗而有力的表现. 我们负责并随后利用从公开的和机构数据集收集的5,910个未加标签的PET/CT扫描的大规模不同培训前群。 我们提议的以块为主的扰动策略鼓励通过分解的遮掩机制来学习代谢和互补解剖表达,在这种机制中,图像块要么被去除(丢失),取而代之的是零值取而代之,要么被取而代之的替代方式取而代之的对应块取而代之. 我们广泛评价了我们提出的整个身体图像重建框架、癌症和非癌症地区的补丁分类以及全身损伤分解。 我们证明,我们的方法比FDG只经过预先训练的模型提高了重建性能,比起DINov3和ResNet50-3D等经过事先训练的既定建筑,在清洁和扰动的成像条件下提高了分类性能,提高了阴道、损伤和解剖区域层面的损伤分化性能。 总而言之,这些结论确定了大规模、多样化的预训数据集的效用,以及我们提议的跨模式自我监督学习战略在丰富、通俗和有力表达全机构PET/CT分析方面的有效性。
